name: Canada
tagline: Transparent entry requirements, high fees, and a study permit queue
summary: In Canada you apply to a named programme, entry requirements are published as IB point thresholds, and admission is far more predictable than in the United States. Education is run by the provinces, so Ontario has one central application system, British Columbia has another, and in Quebec and the other provinces you apply to each university directly. The two catches are money - international undergraduate tuition runs from about CAD 28,000 a year at Manitoba to CAD 66,678 for Commerce at UBC (2026/27) - and immigration, because since 2024 Canada has capped the number of study permit applications it will even look at, and undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to get into that queue.
whyConsider: Entry requirements are published. Universities state the IB points and HL subjects a programme needs, so you can tell in advance whether your predicted score is in range.
Four-year bachelor's degrees with a co-op option at several universities, meaning paid work terms built into the degree - Waterloo is built around it.
A degree from a Canadian university normally leads to a Post-Graduation Work Permit with no field-of-study restriction for bachelor's graduates, which is a clearer route than US OPT.
Both English and French are official languages, and Montreal in particular lets you study in English while living in French.
Class sizes and tuition sit between the European and American extremes, and campuses are safe and well-resourced.

Entry requirements are published as numbers. Universities state the IB points and the Higher Level subjects a programme needs, so you can tell in advance whether your predicted score is in range rather than guessing at a holistic process.
Offers come early and on predicted grades. UBC states plainly that it decides on interim grades and uses the July results only to confirm, which makes the IB calendar a condition rather than a cliff.
A bachelor's degree normally leads to a Post-Graduation Work Permit with no field-of-study restriction, which is a clearer route than US OPT.
Four-year degrees with co-op options at several universities, meaning paid work terms built into the degree. Waterloo is built around it.
watchOuts: The study permit cap. For 2026 Canada set a ceiling of 309,670 study permit application spaces requiring a Provincial Attestation Letter, split by province. Once a province runs out of attestation letters it stops issuing them for the year, so applying early matters more than it should.
Proof of funds. From 1 September 2026 a single applicant must show 23,448 CAD in living costs on top of first-year tuition and travel money. That is money that must visibly exist, not a promise.
Tuition is not capped for internationals and can rise each year. UBC is unusual in guaranteeing increases of no more than 3% a year for four years after you start.
Ontario's central system has no deadline for international applicants - each university sets its own, which sounds relaxed and is actually a trap.
Winters in Montreal, Toronto, Edmonton and Calgary are far harder than a Danish winter. Vancouver and Victoria are mild but very wet.

Do not read one Canadian deadline as Canada's. Toronto and UBC and McGill all close on 15 January 2027; Simon Fraser closes on 31 January, Concordia asks international applicants for 1 February (1 March for others), Alberta sets a date per programme, and Dalhousie closes its health programmes on 15 February and takes the rest as space allows. The province decides the route and the university decides the date.

The mathematics rule is decided two years before you apply. Toronto, UBC and McGill each refuse Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL for their science and business programmes. Dalhousie accepts it. Nothing after DP1 can repair that choice.

Bonus points are counted by some universities and not others. UBC's 24-point floor includes them; Toronto reads your total out of 42 with them excluded. The same predicted grades are three points apart depending on who is reading.

A study permit is not a formality. Undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to enter a capped queue, the 2026 cap was 309,670 applications nationally, and no allocation had been published for 2027 as of September 2026.

Quebec is a second immigration system. A Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec has its own fee, its own financial test and its own processing time, and it has to be granted before the federal permit can be.
Health cover is provincial and Ontario is the province where the answer is no. An international student there is outside the public plan for the whole degree and pays for UHIP instead.

No Ontario university on this page publishes a tuition figure for 2027/28. Toronto says its fees are set in the spring of the year of entry, so a student deciding in January is committing to a price that does not exist yet.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum. Universities set their own and publish them: 24 points at UBC (bonus points included) and Manitoba, 26 at Dalhousie, 28 at York, Toronto Metropolitan, Carleton and Guelph, with competitive programmes asking for more. Toronto reads predicted or final results excluding bonus points. Read each university's IB requirements page.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Canadian universities normally require the full IB Diploma and then name specific Higher Level subjects for the programme - HL Mathematics for engineering, HL Chemistry and Biology for life sciences, and so on. Standard Level subjects usually satisfy prerequisites only where the university says so explicitly.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: There is no single national conversion. Each university maps IB grades onto its own admission average, and Ontario universities also convert IB grades into percentage equivalents for comparison with Ontario's 4U courses.
notes: Transfer credit for HL subjects graded 5 or above is common and can shorten your degree - ask the specific faculty, not general admissions.
Offers are conditional on your final July 2027 results, so a drop below the conditions can cost you the place.

Quebec is different: its universities run a one-year shorter bachelor's for students who completed CEGEP, but international students with a full IB Diploma are normally admitted to the standard programme length. Confirm the programme length with the university before you accept.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The entire English-speaking system - every province except Quebec teaches primarily in English, and Quebec has three large English-language universities (McGill, Concordia, Bishop's).
language.englishProof: Universities generally waive English testing for students educated in English, and an IB Diploma with English A is normally accepted as proof. The exact waiver rule differs by university, so check each one; where a test is required, typical minimums are IELTS 6.5-7.0 or TOEFL iBT 90-100.
notes: In Quebec you can study entirely in English, but daily life, part-time jobs and paperwork are in French. Quebec has its own immigration rules and its own financial requirement for study permits.
French is useful but never required outside Quebec.

feeContext.summary: Canada has no EU or EEA fee category. The line is drawn at Canadian citizenship or permanent residence, so an EU/EEA student pays the full international rate everywhere, with no reciprocal arrangement of any kind.
feeContext.typicalRange: CAD 51,530 to CAD 66,678 a year at UBC in 2026/27, depending on the faculty; CAD 39,007 for a BA at Saskatchewan in 2026/27; about CAD 28,000 on average at Manitoba. Ontario is not established for any year.

The University of Toronto does not publish a tuition figure for the year you would be applying for. Its fees are finalised in the spring of the year of entry, so an applicant deciding in January 2027 is working from the 2026/27 schedule.

livingCostMonthly.note: Derived from the federal immigration minimum of CAD 23,448 for twelve months and rounded. It is the figure you must prove to get a study permit outside Quebec, not a realistic Vancouver or Toronto budget, and it explicitly excludes tuition and travel.

livingContext.livingCostYear: CAD 23,448 for twelve months, for a single applicant outside Quebec applying on or after 1 September 2026. The previous band was CAD 22,895 and the amounts are revised annually, so a figure remembered from an older application is short. Quebec assesses financial capacity itself, through its own immigration ministry and for the CAQ, and the number is different.
livingContext.housing: Most universities guarantee first-year residence only to students who apply by a separate housing deadline, months before term and usually in spring. UBC's is 1 May 2027. Take the guarantee: Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are very expensive and finding a room from Denmark is very hard.
livingContext.healthcare: Provincial, not national, and very different from one province to the next. Ontario excludes international students from the public plan entirely and enrols them in UHIP; British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia admit them on their own conditions, each after a wait; Quebec requires continuous private or public cover for the whole study stay as a condition of the CAQ. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid anywhere in Canada.
livingContext.workRights: A study permit carries work rights during study and the Post-Graduation Work Permit after it. For a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree there is no field-of-study restriction on the PGWP, which is the restriction that applies to non-degree programmes and the clearest practical difference between a university and a college here. Apply within 180 days of confirmation that you completed the programme, and expect to show Canadian Language Benchmarks 7 in English across all four skills.
livingContext.residency: A study permit, not a visa-free stay. Since 2024 Canada caps the number of study permit applications it will process: 309,670 for 2026, allocated by province, with Ontario 104,780, Quebec 93,069, British Columbia 32,596, Alberta 32,271 and Nova Scotia 8,480. Undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to enter that queue and the university requests it after you accept the offer; master's and doctoral students at public institutions stopped needing one on 1 January 2026. No allocation beyond 2026 had been published as of September 2026, so the 2027 position is unknown rather than unchanged. In Quebec, a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec replaces the attestation letter and must be granted before the federal permit.
funding: Entrance scholarships from the university itself, usually awarded from the admission application with no separate form. The exceptions are the large named awards, and they close early: UBC's International Scholars deadline is 15 November 2026, two months before the ordinary application, and McGill's Major Entrance Scholarship closes six days after its application.

The University of Toronto's Lester B. Pearson International Scholarships and UBC's International Scholars programmes are full-cost awards for international students. Both need school nomination in the autumn. Ask your studievejleder in September 2026.
Faculty and programme awards, especially in engineering and commerce, awarded after first year on results.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: There is no Canadian government grant or loan for international undergraduates. Budget on paying tuition from family funds, savings and scholarships.

jurisdictions.name: Ontario
jurisdictions.summary: A system with its own central application service for universities. Applications go through the OUAC, which rations choices by charging for them, and which sets no deadline at all for an applicant from outside Ontario. Ontario also runs a second, separate central service for its 24 colleges.

variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: The one province that excludes international students from the public plan for the whole degree. You are enrolled automatically in UHIP, a not-for-profit plan created by Ontario's universities, it is mandatory, and the premium is billed to your student account. Budget for it as a cost rather than a formality.

sources.title: An international student at an Ontario university does not get the provincial health plan. They are enrolled automatically in the University Health Insurance Plan, a not-for-profit plan created by Ontario's universities, it is mandatory, and the premium is billed to the student account.

variations.label: What applying costs

jurisdictions.name: British Columbia
jurisdictions.summary: One application account covering all 25 public institutions, universities and colleges together, with no limit on choices and nothing charged by the platform. variations.label: Health cover
variations.summary: Compulsory enrolment in the provincial Medical Services Plan for a study permit of six months or more, with a health fee invoiced. Cover starts only after the balance of your arrival month plus two more, so arriving in late August means no provincial cover until 1 November and private insurance until then.

jurisdictions.name: Quebec
jurisdictions.summary: No shared application service and a second immigration system. You apply to each university directly, and before the federal study permit you need a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec with its own fee, its own financial test and its own processing time. Quebec is also the province with a whole extra level of education, the CEGEP, between school and university.

variations.label: Immigration
variations.summary: A Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec is required in addition to the federal study permit and has to be granted first. Quebec assesses your financial capacity itself rather than applying the federal CAD 23,448 figure. This is why Concordia asks international applicants to apply a month before its own deadline.

sources.title: Studying in Quebec requires a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec in addition to the federal study permit, proof of financial capacity assessed by Quebec rather than by IRCC, and health and hospitalisation insurance held continuously for the whole study stay.

variations.summary: Continuous health and hospitalisation insurance for the entire study stay is a condition of the CAQ, not merely a requirement on arrival. Whether you can instead join the Quebec public plan depends on any social security agreement between Quebec and the country where you are insured or hold citizenship, and is not confirmed here; ask the RAMQ or your university.

Studying in Quebec requires a Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec in addition to the federal study permit, proof of financial capacity assessed by Quebec rather than by IRCC, and health and hospitalisation insurance held continuously for the whole study stay.

Quebec places a whole level of education between school and university: 48 public CEGEPs, five of them English-language, plus about 70 private colleges, offering a two-year pre-university programme and a three-year technical programme, both leading to a Diploma of College Studies.

sectorLandscape.summary: Canada divides post-secondary education twice over, and English-language advice usually describes only one half of one division. The first division is the university and the college: four-year degrees against one-to-three-year diplomas, applied through different services even inside the same province, and carrying different post-study work rights. The second is Quebec, which puts a whole extra level between school and university - the CEGEP, two years before a Quebec student even reaches a bachelor's, which is why Quebec degrees are often three years rather than four.

routes.what: The four-year bachelor's degree, awarded by provincially chartered universities. This is what every English-language guide to Canada is describing and what all twenty institutions on this page are. Several build paid work terms into the degree as co-op, which is a Canadian speciality rather than a national rule. A degree also carries the Post-Graduation Work Permit without the field-of-study restriction that applies to shorter programmes, which is a major practical difference between this route and the next one.
routes.note: In Quebec a bachelor's is often three years, because a Quebec student has already spent two years at CEGEP. An IB Diploma holder arriving from abroad takes the longer version. Confirm the length before accepting an offer.

routes.what: Certificates, diplomas, apprenticeships and some degrees, taught for a named occupation rather than a discipline. Ontario alone has 24 of them, and they are applied for through ontariocolleges.ca rather than the OUAC - a different central service for a different sector in the same province. Admission is stated in terms of an Ontario high school diploma, and what that means for an IB Diploma holder from abroad is not published; Ontario's answer is to contact a college directly.
routes.note: Easy to overlook. Two cautions: no college is covered institution by institution on this page, and the Post-Graduation Work Permit rules for non-degree programmes are tighter than for a degree, which is a consequence worth understanding before choosing this route.

routes.localName: polytechnic / institute of technology and advanced learning
routes.what: A name rather than a category. Ontario's own list of its 24 public colleges includes Seneca Polytechnic and two institutions styled Institute of Technology and Advanced Learning alongside the colleges of applied arts and technology, which means a student reading a Canadian polytechnic's website is reading a college's. The name signals a stronger applied-technology and degree-granting emphasis, not a separate legal sector.
routes.note: Whether they differ from the other colleges in anything a student would notice is not covered here.

routes.what: Quebec's own level between school and university, with no equivalent anywhere else in Canada: 48 public CEGEPs, five of them English-language, plus about 70 private colleges. Two programmes lead to a Diploma of College Studies. The pre-university programme takes two years and is the normal Quebec route into a bachelor's degree. The technical programme takes three years, includes at least one workplace placement, and is built to end in a job rather than in a degree. steps: Choose the province before you choose the university, because in Canada the province decides how you apply. Ontario goes through the OUAC, British Columbia through EducationPlannerBC, and Quebec, Alberta and Nova Scotia direct to each university. The three routes have different deadlines, different fees and different numbers of choices.

Check the mathematics rule against your IB subject choices, in DP1 rather than in your final year. Toronto, UBC and McGill each refuse Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL for their science and business programmes; Dalhousie accepts it. Nothing later can repair that choice.

Read the published IB requirement for each programme you want, on the university’s own page. Create the right application account. In Ontario the OUAC charges CAD 159 for three choices and you also pay a document evaluation fee to every separate university. In British Columbia the platform charges nothing and the institution charges its own fee. Applying direct means an account, a fee and a deadline at each university.

Send predicted IB grades and your school transcript. Every Canadian route here decides on predicted results and confirms on final ones, so the offer arrives months before July and is conditional on it.

Accept an offer, pay the deposit, and ask the university to request a Provincial Attestation Letter for you — or, in Quebec, apply for a Certificat d’acceptation du Québec, which is a separate provincial immigration document with its own fee and its own financial test.
Apply for the study permit with the attestation letter or CAQ, your letter of acceptance, proof of CAD 23,448 in living funds outside Quebec plus tuition and travel, and biometrics.

Sort out health cover, which depends on the province and is a separate decision from everything above. Ontario leaves international students outside the public plan for the whole degree; British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia let them in, each on its own terms and each after a wait.
Arrange housing early. Most universities guarantee first-year residence only to students who apply by a separate housing deadline — UBC’s is 1 May 2027.

workRights: Study permit holders may work while studying and after graduating under conditions set on the permit. residency: You need a study permit, not a visa-free stay. Since 2024 Canada caps the number of study permit applications it will process: for 2026 the cap is 309,670 application spaces for people who need a Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter, allocated by province (Ontario 104,780, Quebec 93,069, British Columbia 32,596, down to 1,376 in Prince Edward Island). No allocation beyond 2026 had been published as of September 2026, so treat the 2027 rules as likely-but-unconfirmed and apply as early as you can. housing: Most universities guarantee residence to first-year students who apply by a separate housing deadline, usually in spring. Take the guarantee - Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are very expensive and finding a room from Denmark is very hard. From second year most students share a house or flat, which is where the real cost appears.
healthcare: Health cover depends on the province, and the difference is large. Ontario leaves international students outside the public plan altogether and enrols them in UHIP instead, which is a cost for the whole degree. British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia all admit international students to their provincial plans, each on its own condition and each after a wait during which you need private insurance. notes: The dated milestones on this route are Toronto's, because Toronto is the only Ontario institution in this record whose 2027 calendar was read in full. Waterloo, Queen's, McMaster, Western and Ottawa apply through the same system on their own dates, and those were not established. Do not read Toronto's 15 January as Ontario's.

systems.name: EducationPlannerBC

jurisdiction.authority: EducationPlannerBC, on behalf of British Columbia's public post-secondary institutions

coverage.includes: British Columbia's 25 public post-secondary institutions, universities and colleges alike, from one account. UBC, Simon Fraser and Victoria all state on their own pages that this is the only way in.
coverage.excludes: Private institutions in British Columbia, which apply directly. Coverage of the public sector is the whole sector, which is unusual in this collection and is the reason British Columbia reads as one jurisdiction where Ontario needs two systems for the same province.

choiceRules.note: No limit. You may submit as many applications through the platform as you like, and each institution decides its own. Whether two programmes at one institution take one application or two is set by that institution.

systems.identityRequirement: An EducationPlannerBC account, created with a personal email address. The platform warns specifically against using a school-issued address, because those are deactivated at graduation and the institution's correspondence goes to it.
sharedSteps: Create and confirm the account before you need it - an application cannot be submitted until the confirmation email has been acted on.
Complete the profile, including academic history, once. It is reused across every institution you apply to.
Submit each application with payment. The fee goes to the institution, not to the platform.
systems.decisionModel: Nothing is decided here. EducationPlannerBC passes the application to the institution's own student records system and the institution decides, on its own requirements and its own timetable.
systems.replyModel: Set by each institution. UBC assigns an offer deadline of 1 May or 1 June in the admission letter itself.

notes: One account is not one deadline and not one fee. Both belong to the institution, and the three British Columbia universities in this record charge CAD 130, CAD 184 and CAD 173.25, and close on 15 January, 31 January and a date set per programme.

systems.name: Ontario Universities' Application Centre

jurisdiction.authority: Ontario Universities' Application Centre, a division of the Council of Ontario Universities

coverage.includes: Undergraduate admission to Ontario's publicly assisted universities, including the six listed in this Destination. Every Ontario university in this record applies through it.
coverage.excludes: Ontario's 24 public colleges, which apply through ontariocolleges.ca instead, and consecutive Bachelor of Education and Common Law programmes, which have separate OUAC services. It covers one province, not the country: an applicant to Montreal, Vancouver, Edmonton or Halifax has no business here.

choiceRules.note: The limit of three is per university, not overall. You may apply to as many Ontario universities as you like and to at most three programmes at any one of them, and the choices are not ranked against each other - each is decided on its own. The rationing is by money rather than by number: the base fee covers three choices in total, each further choice costs more, and a Group B applicant also pays a document evaluation fee to every separate university.

systems.identityRequirement: An OUAC account. No national digital identity is involved, which makes this one of the easier portals in this collection to get into from abroad.

fee.note: Base fee for the first three programme choices; CAD 51 for each further choice. Document evaluation fees, charged once per university to Group B applicants, are additional and range from CAD 25 to CAD 200 - CAD 98 at Toronto, CAD 95 at Queen's, Waterloo and McMaster, CAD 93 at Ottawa and CAD 125 at Western.

systems.decisionModel: Each university decides each choice on its own against its own published requirements, and offers are released in rounds from late January through May. There is no provincial ranking, no quota shared between universities and no allocation: two universities can both admit you, or neither.
systems.replyModel: Set by each university in its offer letter rather than by the OUAC. The OUAC's own published response dates - a response by 28 May and no financial commitment required before 1 June - bind universities in respect of Group A applicants only, and a student applying from outside Ontario is Group B.

additionalGuidance.title: More about studying here
additionalGuidance.text: Canada publishes plainly what it wants from an IB student: the points, the Higher Level subjects, the mathematics course that will not do. What it does not publish is a national anything. Education is provincial, so Ontario has a central application service, British Columbia has a different one, and Quebec, Alberta, Nova Scotia, Manitoba and Saskatchewan take you directly. The twenty universities on this page are spread across seven of those provinces, and picking Toronto and picking Vancouver puts a student on two different paths with different deadlines, different fees, different health cover and, in Quebec, a second immigration system on top of the federal one. The money is the other constraint: international undergraduate tuition runs past CAD 50,000 a year at UBC, though Saskatchewan charges CAD 39,007 for a BA in 2026/27 and Manitoba averages about CAD 28,000, and since 2024 the federal government caps how many study permit applications it will even look at.
